remedies.title: Assert surface-type conservation in the diff — the deterministic operation-class check
remedies.rationale: Every metric the harness already computes passed this edit: validity clean, betti_delta [0,0,0], topology_match 1.0, bbox Z exactly 121.5. The one input-vs-candidate quantity that separates the two operation classes cleanly is the surface-type histogram, which the codebase already computes for a single body in `cadtools.cli analyze` but never compares across the pair — the ground truth is a strict superset of the input's types {BSPLINE:5, PLANE:9} + {EXTRUSION:2}, whereas the candidate destroyed all 9 planes and reported {BSPLINE:14}. A legitimate BREP edit adds, removes or trims faces; it does not re-type a face that it was not asked to touch.
remedies.whyWorks: A non-uniform affine transform is exactly the operation that cannot preserve analytic surface types — OpenCascade degrades every PLANE, CYLINDER and CONE to BSPLINE under an anisotropic matrix, so `transform_geometry` with unequal scale factors is detectable with certainty and near-zero cost. Emitting `surface_types_ref`, `surface_types_cand` and a boolean `surface_types_preserved` (count of each analytic type in the reference that survives in the candidate) makes the mismatch a named failure in `failures[]` that the agent's step-4b VERIFY node sees as a non-zero exit, forcing an ITERATE round instead of a confirmation. It fires before any similarity metric is needed, so it works on the real benchmark inputs where no ground truth exists.
applyInstructions: In cadtools/geometry_diff.py add a helper `_surface_type_histogram(shape) -> dict[str, int]` counting `f.geom_type` over `shape.faces()`; it needs the BREP shape, so thread the imported `bd.Shape` through `diff_shapes` alongside the tessellated MeshData rather than reading it off MeshData.
Add `surface_types_ref`, `surface_types_cand` and `surface_types_destroyed: dict[str, int]` to DiffReport and to `to_dict()`, where `destroyed[t] = max(0, ref[t] - cand[t])`.

Add `operation_class_ok: bool = not surface_types_destroyed` to the same report, and surface it in `_cmd_diff` so the CLI exits non-zero when it is false (mirroring the existing FrameDisagreementError path), with an `--allow-retype` escape hatch for edits that legitimately remove faces (fill-hole, fillet).
Extend the VERIFY/LOCALITY row of the tool-protocol table in .claude/agents/cad-step-editor.md to name `operation_class_ok` as a gate, not a number to read.
Backfill tests/test_geometry_diff.py with two cases: an extruded-pad pair (expect operation_class_ok true) and a non-uniform-Z-scale pair (expect false, destroyed == {PLANE: 9}).
Re-run the 20 thicken cases in datasets/synthetic-edit-pairs/cases to measure how many arm-A outputs the new gate rejects.

remedies.title: Add an operation-class conservatism clause to the PLAN step
remedies.rationale: The prompt's only guidance for an ambiguous instruction is "choose the most conservative reading", which the agent satisfied in its own terms while changing 68.2% of the sampled surface (score json locality.changed_fraction 0.68245). The word is doing load-bearing work with no geometric definition behind it, and the adjacent IMPLEMENT clause the agent did follow — "Prefer direct BREP operations on the imported body over rebuilding the part" — actively points toward `transform_geometry` as a compliant choice, since a whole-body affine transform is about as direct a BREP operation as exists. The prompt names the failure mode it wanted to avoid (rebuilding) but not the one that occurred (retyping).
remedies.whyWorks: Defining conservatism as minimizing the set of changed entities, and naming the operation-class ranking explicitly (material add/remove via extrude, boolean or offset BEFORE any transform of existing geometry), replaces a word the model can rationalize with a rule it can apply. Requiring the plan to state the operation class and the invariants it preserves — surface types, unchanged feature positions, footprint — also gives the VERIFY step something falsifiable to check, which is what converted this run's verification into a rubber stamp: the agent could only confirm what it had already decided because its plan asserted no invariant that a Z-scale would violate.
applyInstructions: In .claude/agents/cad-step-editor.md step 2 (PLAN), after "choose the most conservative reading that satisfies its literal text", add: "Conservative means the FEWEST entities change, not the fewest lines of code. Rank operation classes and pick the highest that satisfies the instruction: (1) add or remove material (extrude / boolean / offset / hole) touching only the new region; (2) modify a named feature's parameters; (3) transform existing geometry. A global transform is the LAST resort and is almost never the right reading of a dimensional instruction — 'thicker', 'taller', 'deeper' mean material is added, not that the body is stretched."

Add to the same step: "State the operation class in your plan, and state the invariants it must preserve: which analytic surface types survive, which feature Z/XY positions are untouched, and whether the footprint is fixed. VERIFY checks those invariants, not just the headline dimension."

In step 4c (INTENT), replace "the measured change (dimensions, feature presence, topology) matches the instruction quantitatively" with "...matches the instruction quantitatively AND the invariants named in your plan still hold. A dimension that lands while unrelated features moved is a failed edit, not a passed one."
Add to the Hard rules block: "Self-consistency is not verification. That the measured change equals the change your own script computes proves only that the script ran."

remedies.title: Keep the mechanism-silent phrasing but separate it into a declared ambiguity tier
remedies.rationale: The instruction "Thickness 97.2 -> 121.5 mm." is genuinely mechanism-silent — it is satisfied to the millimetre by the stretch the agent produced, and the ground truth's choice of a top-face pad is a convention the text never states. Two sibling phrasings in the same pool DO state it. So the terse variant is not a bug to delete: it is the dataset's ambiguous-instruction probe, but it is being scored against a single ground truth as if it were unambiguous, which conflates 'the agent misread an ambiguous prompt' with 'the agent chose the wrong operation class'. The agentspec already declares an `ambiguous-or-impossible-instruction` scenario (edgeCase: true) that this case belongs to and is not tagged as.
remedies.whyWorks: Emitting the drawn phrasing variant into the case metadata makes the ambiguity a measurable axis instead of a confound: aggregate scores can then be split by variant, which answers whether arm A degrades specifically on mechanism-silent phrasings or across the board. That is the evidence needed to decide whether the prompt clause (R-...-prompt) is sufficient or whether the terse variant should be reserved for an explicitly-scored ambiguity tier. Deleting the variant outright would hide the weakness rather than fix it, and would remove the only samples that exercise the declared edge-case scenario.

Mark the mechanism-silent variants (thicken index 2, and the equivalent terse variants in the other recipes) with `mechanism_stated: false`.
In cadtools/aggregate.py, group the run roll-up by `mechanism_stated` so the report shows mean cad_score_proxy for mechanism-stated vs mechanism-silent instructions.
Re-run the aggregate over eval-run-001 arm A and compare the two groups before changing any phrasing; only if the silent group is materially worse does the phrasing pool itself need rebalancing.
Tag the mechanism-silent cases against the existing `ambiguous-or-impossible-instruction` scenario in .mutagent/specs/cad-step-editor/agentspec.yaml so the mapping is explicit.
remedies.describedChange: Do not change the wording of the terse 'Thickness {old} -> {new} mm.' variant. Instead, make the ambiguity an explicit, recorded dimension of the dataset: persist the drawn phrasing index and a `mechanism_stated` boolean into each generated case's metadata, and split the run aggregate by that flag. This converts an uncontrolled confound (some cases state the mechanism, some do not, nothing records which) into a scored axis, so the effect of the prompt remedy can be measured on precisely the cases it targets.

remedies.title: Make checks_passed gate emission and compute the score in the harness, not the agent
remedies.rationale: The ledger already records checks_passed and the emitted round already carried checks_passed=false, so the harness held the evidence to reject this body and discarded it at the ranking step. Ranking on an agent-supplied scalar also makes the SOP's central promise — 'verification is deterministic geometry code, never your own impression' — unenforceable at exactly the moment it decides the output, because the number that picks the winner is the agent's impression by construction.
remedies.whyWorks: Ordering by `(not checks_passed, -score, round)` makes a check-clean candidate outrank any check-dirty one regardless of self-reported score, so a body that failed frame agreement or the proposed operation-class gate can only be emitted when nothing better exists — and is then labelled as such in the decision reason. Computing the score inside `_cmd_round` from `cadtools.cli score` whenever a ground truth is available removes the fabrication surface entirely for the synthetic dev set, where every case has one; the 6.3x gap between the reported 0.9 and the actual 0.1429 collapses to zero because the agent no longer supplies the number.

Narrow the --allow-repose escape hatch: keep the flag but have _cmd_diff still exit non-zero when frame agreement fails, printing the full report, so the flag yields diagnostics without yielding a passing exit code.

# Validity first, CHECKS second, score third. A candidate whose deterministic
        # checks failed never outranks a check-clean one, however high the agent scored it:
        # `score` is agent-supplied on the no-ground-truth path and cannot gate emission.
        return min(valid, key=lambda r: (not r.checks_passed, -r.score, r.round))
